Soil heat flux

Source: R/metric-soil-heat.R
ef_g.Rd

Estimates the instantaneous soil heat flux \(G\) at the satellite overpass, i.e. the part of the net radiation \(R_n\) conducted into the ground, with an empirical relation between the ratio \(G/R_n\) and surface variables. \(G\) is the second term of the METRIC surface energy balance \(LE = R_n - G - H\).

  • ef_g() is the dispatcher: it calls the method chosen with method (no default), derives \(G/R_n\), builds the diagnostic flags and records the provenance.

  • ef_g_bastiaanssen() evaluates the SEBAL relation of Bastiaanssen (2000) as a function of surface temperature, albedo and NDVI.

  • ef_g_tasumi() evaluates the relation attributed to Tasumi (2003) and used in METRIC as a function of LAI, with a bare-soil branch for LAI < 0.5.

The method functions are purely arithmetic and return \(G\) only.

Usage

ef_g(rn, lst = NULL, albedo = NULL, ndvi = NULL, lai = NULL, method)

ef_g_bastiaanssen(rn, lst, albedo, ndvi)

ef_g_tasumi(rn, lst, lai)

Arguments

rn

Numeric. Net radiation \(R_n\) at the satellite overpass [W m-2], positive towards the surface (e.g. from ef_net_radiation()). Any finite value is accepted; negative values are physically possible.

lst

Numeric. Land surface temperature \(T_s\) [K]. Must be finite and > 0. Converted internally to degrees Celsius with the package constant 273.15 K. For ef_g_tasumi() it is required in every position, not only where the bare-soil branch applies (see Details).

albedo

Numeric. Broadband surface albedo \(\alpha\) [-]. Must lie in [0, 1].

ndvi

Numeric. Normalised difference vegetation index [-]. Must lie in [-1, 1].

lai

Numeric. Leaf area index [m2 m-2]. Must be finite and >= 0.

method

Character. The formulation, with no default: the choice of \(G\) is a scientific decision that must be explicit. One of "bastiaanssen" (requires lst, albedo, ndvi) or "tasumi" (requires lst, lai). Matched exactly (no abbreviation, no change of case). Arguments not used by the chosen method are ignored.

Value

ef_g_bastiaanssen() and ef_g_tasumi() return a numeric vector of soil heat flux \(G\) [W m-2] with the common length of the inputs, keeping the dim of matrix or array inputs. Negative values and values larger than rn are possible and returned unchanged.

ef_g() returns a list of class earthflux_soil_heat_flux with elements:

g

\(G\) [W m-2], identical to the method function.

g_rn_ratio

\(G/R_n\) [-], computed as g / rn; NA where rn is 0.

method

The method name.

branch

For "tasumi", a character vector with the branch applied in each position ("lai_ge_0.5" or "lai_lt_0.5"; NA where g is NA), with the shape of g; NULL for "bastiaanssen".

flags

A list of diagnostic flag records (see Diagnostics).

provenance

A list with the method, the method function, the verification status, the references, the Kelvin offset, the coefficients of the equation, the inputs used, the flag codes evaluated (flags_evaluated) and the EarthFlux version.

Details

Bastiaanssen (SEBAL). $$\frac{G}{R_n} = T_c \, (0.0038 + 0.0074\,\alpha)\, (1 - 0.98\,\mathrm{NDVI}^4), \qquad G = R_n \frac{G}{R_n}$$ with \(T_c = T_s - 273.15\) in degrees Celsius. The ratio is negative for \(T_s < 273.15\) K and NDVI enters with an even power, so negative NDVI (water) gives the same result as the opposite positive NDVI.

Tasumi (METRIC). $$\frac{G}{R_n} = 0.05 + 0.18\, e^{-0.521\,\mathrm{LAI}}, \qquad G = R_n \frac{G}{R_n} \qquad (\mathrm{LAI} \ge 0.5)$$ $$G = 1.80\, T_c + 0.084\, R_n \qquad (\mathrm{LAI} < 0.5)$$ The bare-soil branch is evaluated directly, without dividing by \(R_n\). The relation is discontinuous at LAI = 0.5, which belongs to the vegetated branch. Missing lst gives a missing \(G\) in both branches (decision G-D5, provisional), so the result does not depend on which branch a position falls in.

Assumptions: \(G\) and \(R_n\) are instantaneous at the overpass; \(G > 0\) when heat flows from the surface into the ground. Both relations are empirical, developed for land surfaces near midday; no rule is applied for water, snow or impervious surfaces, which must be masked or treated separately by the user.

Inputs. Arguments must be numeric and have length 1 or a common length; length-1 arguments are recycled; matrix or array arguments must share their dim and are not recycled. Missing values (NA, NaN) propagate to the corresponding output element without errors or warnings. Physically impossible values (albedo outside [0, 1], ndvi outside [-1, 1], negative lai, non-positive lst, or any infinite value) raise an error of class earthflux_domain_error (also earthflux_input_error) naming the argument; values are never corrected. A missing or unknown method raises earthflux_missing_input or earthflux_unknown_method, and an input required by the chosen method that is missing or NULL raises earthflux_missing_input (all also earthflux_input_error).

Diagnostics. ef_g() returns, in flags, one record per condition that holds in at least one position: EF_INPUT_NA (a required input is missing), EF_G_RN_NONPOSITIVE (\(R_n \le 0\)), EF_G_RATIO_NEGATIVE (\(G/R_n < 0\)), EF_G_AVAILABLE_NONPOSITIVE (\(R_n - G \le 0\)) and, for "tasumi", EF_G_LOW_LAI_BRANCH (bare-soil branch applied). No plausible range of \(G/R_n\) is checked until one is documented with a reference.

Verification status

"bastiaanssen" is VERIFICADA (SEBAL-Idaho 2002): Waters et al. (2002), p. 24, Eq. 24, after Bastiaanssen (2000), print \(G/R_n = T_s/\alpha\, (0.0038\,\alpha + 0.0074\,\alpha^2)\, (1 - 0.98\,\mathrm{NDVI}^4)\) with \(T_s\) in degrees Celsius, "representing values near midday"; the expanded form above is algebraically identical for \(\alpha > 0\) (and defined at \(\alpha = 0\)). The manual assigns G/Rn = 0.5 to water (NDVI < 0) and to snow (\(T_s\) < 4 degrees C and albedo > 0.45) (p. 25, appendix 10); these rules are not applied here (decision G-D4). The cross-check with Allen et al. (2007) remains desirable but is no longer blocking.

"tasumi" is CANDIDATA: its form, coefficients and the LAI threshold were observed in a secondary implementation (the water R package, version 1.0) and are rewritten here; the primary references (Tasumi, 2003; Allen et al., 2007) were not consulted. Whether its bare-soil condition is LAI < 0.5 or LAI <= 0.5 remains to be verified.

The method has no default (dispatcher convention, decision T-15). Applying the relations to 1 km MODIS pixels (mixed cover, composite NDVI and LAI) is not validated.

References

Bastiaanssen, W. G. M. (2000). SEBAL-based sensible and latent heat fluxes in the irrigated Gediz Basin, Turkey. Journal of Hydrology, 229(1-2), 87-100. doi:10.1016/S0022-1694(99)00202-4

Tasumi, M. (2003). Progress in operational estimation of regional evapotranspiration using satellite imagery (PhD dissertation). University of Idaho.

Allen, R. G., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2007). Satellite-based energy balance for mapping evapotranspiration with internalized calibration (METRIC) - Model. Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering, 133(4), 380-394. doi:10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9437(2007)133:4(380)

Waters, R., Allen, R., Bastiaanssen, W., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2002). SEBAL: Surface Energy Balance Algorithms for Land. Idaho implementation. Advanced training and users manual (Version 1.0). University of Idaho and Idaho Department of Water Resources.

See also

ef_net_radiation() for \(R_n\).

Examples

# Tasumi: dense canopy (vegetated branch) and bare soil (LAI < 0.5)
ef_g_tasumi(rn = c(550, 400), lst = c(300, 318.15), lai = c(3, 0.2))
#> [1]  48.24115 114.60000

# Bastiaanssen: intermediate vegetation
ef_g_bastiaanssen(rn = 500, lst = 303.15, albedo = 0.20, ndvi = 0.50)
#> [1] 74.349

# Dispatcher: G, G/Rn, branch, flags and provenance
g <- ef_g(rn = c(550, 40), lst = 318.15, lai = c(3, 0.2),
          method = "tasumi")
g$g
#> [1] 48.24115 84.36000
g$g_rn_ratio
#> [1] 0.08771119 2.10900000
g$branch
#> [1] "lai_ge_0.5" "lai_lt_0.5"
vapply(g$flags, `[[`, character(1), "code")
#> [1] "EF_G_AVAILABLE_NONPOSITIVE" "EF_G_LOW_LAI_BRANCH"       

# Chained with the net radiation
rn <- ef_net_radiation(rs_in = 800, albedo = 0.20, rl_in = 320,
                       rl_out = 450.0846, emissivity = 0.98)
ef_g(rn, lst = 303.15, albedo = 0.20, ndvi = 0.50,
     method = "bastiaanssen")$g
#> [1] 74.87173
